data.name: Ginnifer
data.gender_notes: Ginnifer is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word γυνηφορός (gynēphorós), meaning ‘woman-bearer’ or ‘bringer of women’. The name Ginnifer may be a variant of Guinevere or Gwendolyn, both meaning ‘fair one’ or ‘white wave’. The name Ginnifer carries the meaning “Fair, beautiful” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Ginnifer usually hope their child will grow to embody fair, beautiful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of beauty, grace, and femininity.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ginnifer total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

It carries a strong sense of signifies femininity, strength, and maternal niceties. Women named Ginnifer commonly evoke feelings of beauty, grace, and power, making it a befitting name for romantic characters and exuding an aura of mystery and enchantment.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, the name Ginnifer represents the divine feminine and the nurturing, creative power of women. It highlights the importance of feminine energy in our lives, emphasizing the intangible yet powerful role women play in creating, sustaining, and raising future generations. In a more metaphysical sense, the name can serve as a reminder of the divine energy within all women, inspiring them to embrace their inner strength, beauty, and creativity.
